Double tG relative to injection 6 while holding the other settings fixed to test whether a shallower gradient resolves its crowded middle and late peaks. This retains the successful early-pair separation and should keep the last peak near the 10-minute target.

Keep the improved gradient from injection 9 and raise temperature to probe selectivity for the persistent close pair, which did not improve with a shallower gradient. Higher temperature should also bring the last peak below 10 minutes.

Increase temperature one grid step while preserving the best gradient to shift the sole unresolved pair away from its near-coelution at 35 C. This may achieve full resolution while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Make the gradient one step shallower at the best temperature to try to lift the sole remaining critical pair from R = 1.20 above 1.5. The current last-peak time of 8.59 minutes provides some room for increased retention before the time penalty becomes significant.

Increase gradient slope slightly from 0.040 to 0.0417 organic fraction per minute, preserving most of injection 12's resolution margin while accelerating the last peak. This should bring the last peak just below 10 minutes and keep the critical pair above R = 1.5.

Injection 13 already achieves the maximum CRF; test a slightly steeper slope, 0.04375 versus 0.04167 per minute, to shorten elution while retaining full resolution. Despite the longer programmed tG, the last peak should elute earlier, with the critical pair predicted to remain just above R = 1.5.

With the maximum CRF secured, test a 10 C temperature increase at the same gradient to seek a shorter fully resolved run. This probes a new selectivity regime, since further steepening at 40 C would likely push the critical pair below R = 1.5.

Test a steeper gradient at 50 C to shorten the run and potentially separate the remaining close pair, whose elution order appears to have reversed between 40 and 50 C. Keep injection 14 as the shortest confirmed fully resolved method.

Shift the gradient window down by 0.05 while preserving injection 16's slope and temperature to test solvent-window selectivity for the remaining close pair. The 7.02-minute last-peak time leaves room for added retention while seeking a faster fully resolved alternative to injection 14.

Test higher-temperature selectivity with injection 17's gradient to move the persistent close pair farther past its apparent elution-order crossover and shorten retention. The lower starting organic fraction provides extra retention for the early peaks as temperature rises.

Test the midpoint temperature to balance the competing critical pairs: the later pair improves with temperature, while the earlier pair loses resolution. Interpolation between injections 17 and 18 suggests both may exceed R = 1.5 at 55 C, with the last peak below 8 minutes.

Flatten the gradient at 55 C to improve the remaining early critical pair while retaining the later pair's resolution margin. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially yielding another fully resolved method with maximum CRF.

Increase the gradient slope modestly from 0.04375 to 0.046875 per minute to shorten the fully resolved 55 C method. Interpolation from injections 19 and 20 suggests both critical pairs should remain above R = 1.5, with the last peak near 9 minutes.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve the early critical pair while steepening the gradient to shorten the run. This tests whether solvent-window selectivity can preserve full resolution at a faster slope than injection 21.

Increase the slope modestly from 0.060 to 0.065 per minute to shorten the fastest confirmed fully resolved method. The earlier critical pair has some resolution margin, while the later pair has shown little sensitivity to slope at 55 C.

Lower the starting organic fraction to support the early critical pair while increasing the slope to 0.075 per minute. This tests a potentially faster fully resolved method, retaining injection 23 as the shortest confirmed maximum-CRF result.

Use the final injection to test a slightly steeper slope of 0.080 per minute, seeking earlier elution while checking the resolution boundary. The early critical pair may fall below 1.5; injection 24 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method with maximum CRF.
